summary.intent: Run a comprehensive cryptographic security review of all changes on the feat/store-ipns-crypto-data-in-db branch, then fix identified high and medium severity issues and push to remote.
summary.outcome: The security review was completed and the report was committed. The session was interrupted before the high/medium issues could be fixed and pushed; the transcript ends after committing the report with the user requesting fixes.

repo: Project uses a zero-knowledge architecture: server never has plaintext keys, IPNS keys encrypted with TEE public key, signing happens client-side
Key hierarchy: rootFolderKey → folderKey → fileKey, all wrapped with ECIES
SDK-core and apps/web can diverge in implementation — a base64 spread-operator fix was applied to SDK-core but not backported to the web app
pubKey-to-ipnsName binding is enforced on resolve (client-side) but not server-side; first-write immutability is the mitigation
Branch is feat/store-ipns-crypto-data-in-db, ~4 commits, ~30 files changed

code.finding: Spread operator used for base64 encoding will cause call-stack overflow on large records; SDK-core already has this fixed but web app does not
publicKey is not sent on publish, making the pubKey-to-ipnsName binding verification dead code for web-published records

workflow: Parallel sub-agents were used to review different areas (API crypto, SDK crypto, e2e tests) simultaneously before compiling into a single report
The security:review command is protected from GSD updates to preserve its integrity

friction: Session was interrupted mid-task by a usage quota limit ('You're out of extra usage · resets Apr 3 at 6pm (Europe/Berlin)'), requiring the user to manually prompt resumption
open_items: Fix HIGH: spread operator base64 encoding crash in apps/web/src/services/ipns.service.ts:54

Fix MEDIUM: no server-side publicKey-to-ipnsName binding (currently only defense-in-depth via first-write immutability and client-side check)
Mark resolved findings in the security report with the fix commit references
